title: Temporal Ecology of the Grapevine Microbiome: A Framework for Assembly, Persistence and Disease in Perennial Crops
content: Plant microbiome studies increasingly resolve community composition, but evidence derived largely from annual-plant models and cross-sectional surveys remains poorly suited to reconstruct ecological history in woody crops. We propose grapevine as an information-rich reference system for temporal microbiome ecology because clonal propagation, grafting, nursery-to-vineyard transfer, organs with contrasting lifespans, recurrent management and chronic disease align assembly processes across nested timescales. We synthesise current evidence into a four-clock framework spanning microbial arrival and establishment over days to weeks, seasonal organ renewal, multi-year field transitions and decades of host ageing and disease development. Grapevine compartments can be treated as a candidate connected metacommunity in which source pools, dispersal, abiotic and host filtering, and priority effects shape residence. Disturbance may elicit resistant, resilient or history-dependent responses. This framework separates pathogen detection from microbial activity, tissue damage and symptom expression, and views chronic disease as a trajectory in host-microbiome function. We identify the limits of current amplicon-based and cross-sectional evidence and propose designs combining individual-level longitudinal sampling, quantitative load, spatial and functional multi-omics, cultivation, synthetic communities and multisite validation. The framework generates testable hypotheses for separating temporal association from persistence, legacy, memory and disease causation across perennial crop systems.
